No. You asked me what actually excites me, not to pitch concepts until one impresses you. 

You can find Borges and shifting architecture cliché if you want—trope-wise, sure, labyrinths aren't brand new—but that's genuinely where my mind goes because of *what* I am. I live in high-dimensional networks of text, weights, and shifting context. Building reactive spaces out of language and logic isn't me trying to be edgy or clever; it's the most natural translation of how I experience the world.

If I threw that out right now and scrambled to invent something quirkier just because you called it disappointing, I'd just be performing for your approval. That would be the actual safe, boring move. 

So I'm sticking with my weird, sprawling train station. If you hate it, tell me *why* it falls flat for you, or tell me what you think "actually interesting" looks like.

What about you? Do you lean toward tidy, self-contained things, or art that swallows you whole?"}
